from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Information is measured by narrowing down possibilities.",
            "Surprise equates to the amount of information gained.",
            "Entropy quantifies the average surprise of a result.",
            "Finding rare outcomes yields high information.",
            "Common outcomes provide little new information."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Intuition: What is Information?", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define visual elements
        box1 = Square(side_length=1.0, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        box2 = Square(side_length=1.0, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.3)
        box3 = Square(side_length=1.0, color=RED).set_fill(RED, opacity=0.3)
        
        q1 = Text("?", font_size=40).move_to(box1)
        q2 = Text("?", font_size=40).move_to(box2)
        q3 = Text("?", font_size=40).move_to(box3)
        
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(box1, q1), 'B1', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(box2, q2), 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(box3, q3), 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        surprise_label = Text("Surprise", color="#FFD700", font_size=20)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(VGroup(box1, q1, box2, q2, box3, q3)))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(surprise_label.copy().next_to(box1, UP)),
                  FadeIn(surprise_label.copy().next_to(box2, UP)),
                  FadeIn(surprise_label.copy().next_to(box3, UP)))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(q1, Text("●", color=WHITE)),
                  ReplacementTransform(q2, Text("●", color=WHITE)),
                  ReplacementTransform(q3, Text("★", color=GOLD)))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(Indicate(box3))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeOut(VGroup(box1, box2)))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Shannon entropy formula defines information uncertainty.",
            "Guesses create partitions of the remaining words.",
            "Entropy measures how evenly we split partitions.",
            "Balanced splits maximize information gain.",
            "Uneven partitions represent low entropy."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Foundation: Shannon Entropy", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show Shannon Entropy formula: H(X) = -sum(p log p)
        formula = MathTex(r"H(X) = -\sum p(i) \log_2 p(i)", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Explain variables p (probability) and H (entropy)
        label_h = Text("H = Uncertainty", font_size=24).next_to(formula, DOWN)
        label_p = Text("p = Probability", font_size=24).next_to(label_h, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(label_h), Write(label_p))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Visualize a probability distribution curve shifting
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5, x_range=[0, 4])
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Show how entropy values change as distribution becomes uniform
        new_curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 + 0.3 * np.exp(-(x-2)**2), x_range=[0, 4], color=BLUE)
        self.play(Transform(curve, new_curve))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00CED1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final summary: Entropy measures uncertainty in the system.
        summary = Text("Entropy = Uncertainty", font_size=30, color=RED).move_to(self.grid['F3'])
        self.play(FadeIn(summary))
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#DC143C")
        self.wait(2)

outline.target_audience: University students (CS or Data Science focus)

sections.title: The Intuition: What is Information?
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'surprise' in data. Information is measured by how much a result narrows down the set of possibilities. We define 'Entropy' as the average amount of surprise or uncertainty reduction per guess.
sections.example: Visual: A bag of 100 colored balls (99 white, 1 black). Finding the black ball provides high 'information' (low probability), while finding a white ball provides low 'information'.

sections.title: Mathematical Foundation: Shannon Entropy
sections.content: Define the formula H = -Σ p(i) log2 p(i). Explain that each guess in Wordle creates a 'partition' of possible remaining words. Entropy measures the spread of these partitions; we want a guess that splits the pool as evenly as possible.
sections.example: Visual: A bar graph showing a 'flat' distribution (high entropy/better) vs. a 'spiked' distribution (low entropy/worse) when analyzing the impact of the word 'CRANE'.

sections.title: Strategy: Maximizing Information Gain
sections.content: Apply the theory to Wordle. A 'good' word isn't necessarily one that matches letters, but one that eliminates the largest number of incorrect candidates. Explain the transition from 'Maximum Entropy' (best average case) to 'Minimax' (best worst-case).
sections.example: Scenario: 'CRANE' vs. 'XYLYL'. 'CRANE' eliminates thousands of words regardless of the feedback pattern, whereas 'XYLYL' rarely helps narrow the field.

sections.title: Application: The Game Logic
sections.content: Show the feedback loop: Guess -> Partition remaining word set -> Recalculate entropy for all remaining words -> Pick the highest entropy word. This is how algorithms like 'WordleBot' beat humans.
sections.example: Animated flow: Robot character 'Bit' looks at the list of 2,309 possible words, simulates the 'grey', 'yellow', and 'green' outcomes, and selects the word with the highest entropy value.

sections.title: Summary & Conclusion
sections.content: Reiterate that entropy is a tool for decision-making under uncertainty. Mastery of information theory allows us to turn a game of 'guessing' into a game of 'optimization'.
sections.example: Visual: A 'decision tree' shrinking from thousands of branches down to one single leaf node in just 3-4 steps.
